lessons.title: Data Commander Overview — Tổng quan Analytics
lessons.objective: Understand data maturity levels và the 4-level analytics framework
lessons.content:
Data Commander = bộ não số của PSN. Without data, you're flying blind. With data, you see 6 months ahead.

DATA MATURITY LEVELS:

LEVEL 1: NO DATA (Trực giác)
- Leader makes decisions by gut feeling
- 'I think recruits are down'
- 'This approach feels right'
- Risk: Wrong decisions, can't track progress, can't learn

LEVEL 2: BASIC TRACKING (Số liệu)
- Recording what happened
- Spreadsheet with member list, orders, recruits
- 'We had 5 recruits last month'
- Risk: Reactive only, can't predict, manual data entry

LEVEL 3: ANALYTICS (Phân tích)
- Understanding WHY things happened
- Trends, patterns, correlations
- 'Recruits dropped because we reduced connects from 10 to 5'
- Risk: Still manual, insights not always actionable

LEVEL 4: PREDICTIVE AI (Dự báo)
- Predicting WHAT will happen
- Automated alerts, forecasts, recommendations
- 'Based on current trend, we'll hit 50 members by September'
- Risk: Requires tech investment

Target: Reach Level 3 within Module 11. Level 4 as ongoing evolution.

4 ANALYTICS LEVELS (Davenport Framework):

1. DESCRIPTIVE — What happened?
Examples:
- 'We recruited 5 members last month'
- 'Revenue was 12M VND'
- 'PSN has 30 active members'
Tool: Reports, dashboards, spreadsheets

2. DIAGNOSTIC — Why did it happen?
Examples:
- 'Recruits dropped because we stopped daily connects'
- 'Revenue up because of flash sale campaign'
- 'Members active because of weekly meetings'
Tool: Drill-down analysis, root cause analysis

3. PREDICTIVE — What will happen?
Examples:
- 'At current connect rate, we'll recruit 8 members this month'
- 'Based on seasonality, July will be slow'
- 'Member X is at risk of leaving'
Tool: Trend analysis, forecasting models, risk scoring

4. PRESCRIPTIVE — What should we do?
Examples:
- 'Increase connects to 15/day to hit 10 recruits'
- 'Run retention campaign for 5 at-risk members'
- 'Shift budget from FB to Zalo DMs'
Tool: Decision frameworks, optimization algorithms

METRIC HIERARCHY:

Level 1: North Star Metric
- ONE metric that defines PSN health
- For Droppii: 'Weekly Active Revenue Producers'
- Everything else supports or explains this

Level 2: Supporting Metrics (4-6 metrics)
- Recruitment: Connects/day, presentations/day
- Retention: Weekly active rate, habit score
- Revenue: AOV, order frequency, customer NPS
- Team: Sub-leader count, PSN health score

Level 3: Detailed Metrics (10-20 metrics)
- Per-member: Connects, orders, habit score, engagement
- Per-channel: Response rate, conversion rate, ROI
- Per-campaign: Reach, engagement, conversion, ROI

Level 4: Raw Data (Unlimited)
- Every connect, every order, every message
- Used for trend analysis and model building

DATA CULTURE:

Building data culture trong PSN:

1. LEAD WITH DATA
Leader references data in every PSN meeting:
- 'Last week we had 200 connects with 15% response rate'
- 'Our target: 250 connects with 20% response'
- 'Let's figure out how to get there'

2. MAKE DATA VISIBLE
- Dashboard displayed in PSN group (weekly update)
- Metrics on wall at offline meetings
- Public tracking: leaderboard for connects, orders

3. CELEBRATE DATA WINS
- 'Trang hit 50 connects this week — up from 30 last week!'
- 'Our response rate improved from 12% to 18%'
- Make data improvement exciting

4. ASK DATA QUESTIONS
- 'Why did response rate drop this week?'
- 'What drove the revenue spike?'
- 'Who improved the most this month?'

5. ACT ON DATA
- Data without action = wasted effort
- Every insight should lead to 1 action
- Track: Insight → Action → Result

Action items:
1. Assess your current data maturity (Level 1-4)
2. Define your North Star Metric
3. List 4-6 supporting metrics you currently track
4. Plan upgrade path from current level to Level 3

lessons.title: Metrics Framework — Chọn metrics đúng
lessons.objective: Learn to select, categorize, and prioritize the right metrics for PSN
lessons.content:
Wrong metrics = wrong decisions. Right metrics = competitive advantage.

METRIC SELECTION PRINCIPLES:

1. ACTIONABLE: Can you influence this metric by doing something?
✅ Actionable: 'Connect rate' — you can improve it by training
❌ Not actionable: 'Economy downturn' — you can't control it

2. MEASURABLE: Can you track it accurately and consistently?
✅ Measurable: 'Orders per week' — exact count
❌ Hard to measure: 'Brand awareness' — vague, hard to quantify

3. RELEVANT: Does this metric drive your North Star?
✅ Relevant: 'Connects per day' → drives recruits → drives revenue
❌ Irrelevant: 'Number of Facebook likes' → doesn't drive anything specific

4. TIMELY: Can you get this data frequently enough to act on it?
✅ Timely: 'Daily connects' — you see results daily
❌ Too slow: 'Monthly revenue' — you only know results after month ends

VANITY vs ACTIONABLE METRICS:

VANITY METRICS (Looks good, not useful):
- Facebook likes/followers: 'We have 1000 followers!' But 0 orders?
- Post reach: '10K people saw our post!' But 0 engagement?
- App downloads: '100 downloads!' But 0 active users?
- Event attendance: '50 people came!' But 0 follow-up?

Rule: If metric goes UP but business doesn't improve, it's vanity.

ACTIONABLE METRICS (Drive decisions):
- Connect rate: '15% response rate — let's improve to 20%'
- Conversion rate: '10% of connects become customers — let's improve to 15%'
- Revenue per member: '200K/week per member — let's get to 300K'
- Weekly active rate: '70% active — let's get to 85%'

LEADING vs LAGGING INDICATORS:

LEADING INDICATORS (Predict future):
- Connects per day → predicts future recruits
- Engagement rate → predicts future retention
- Presentation count → predicts future revenue
- Habit score → predicts member longevity

Rule: Track leading indicators MORE than lagging. Leading gives you time to fix. Lagging only tells you after damage is done.

LAGGING INDICATORS (Measure past):
- Revenue (last month)
- Member count (current)
- Orders (this week)
- Retention rate (last quarter)

METRIC BALANCE SCORECARD:

Balanced metrics cover 4 perspectives:

1. CUSTOMER (Recruitment + Retention):
- New recruits/month
- Active member rate
- Habit score average
- NPS (Net Promoter Score)

2. INTERNAL (Operations):
- Connects/day per member
- Presentation/week
- Event attendance
- PSN meeting participation

3. FINANCIAL:
- Revenue/month
- Orders/month
- AOV (Average Order Value)
- Cost per acquisition

4. GROWTH (Development):
- Sub-leader count
- New PSNs created
- Training completion rate
- Leader pipeline depth

THE ONE METRIC THAT MATTERS:

Your North Star Metric:
The ONE metric that, if it goes up, everything else is fine.

For a Droppii MLM PSN:
- North Star: 'Weekly Active Revenue Producers'
= Members who do BOTH (connect AND order) in the last 7 days

Why this metric:
- Connects without orders = recruiting activity, no revenue
- Orders without connects = one-time customers, no growth
- Both = healthy, growing PSN

Action items:
1. Define your North Star Metric (1 sentence)
2. List 4-6 actionable metrics you'll track weekly
3. Audit current metrics: eliminate vanity, add actionable
4. Set up weekly metrics review ritual

lessons.title: Data Collection System — Hệ thống thu thập dữ liệu
lessons.objective: Build systematic data collection process without becoming a data-entry clerk
lessons.content:
Data collection = foundation of analytics. But you're not a data entry clerk. Automate where possible.

DATA COLLECTION STRATEGY:

AUTOMATED (Priority):
- Revenue: Droppii app → auto-export to spreadsheet
- Orders: Droppii order history → weekly export
- App activity: Login, orders, habit score from app
- Social metrics: Engagement from Zalo/FB insights
- PSN metrics: Dashboard from Mekong CLI

SEMI-AUTOMATED:
- Connects: Member self-reporting (weekly form)
- Presentations: Member self-reporting (weekly form)
- Habit score: Auto-calculated from activity data
- Team meetings: Leader notes in template

MANUAL (Minimize):
- Qualitative feedback: Weekly 1:1 notes
- Observations: Leader's notes on member energy
- Strategic insights: Leader's reflection

RECRUITMENT:

| ... | | | | |
| TOTAL | ___ | ___ | ___ | ___% |

REVENUE:
| Member | Orders/week | Revenue/week | AOV | New customers |
|--------|-------------|--------------|-----|---------------|
| [Name] | ___ | ___K | ___K | ___ |
| ... | | | | |
| TOTAL | ___K | ___K | ___K | ___ |

ENGAGEMENT:
| Member | PSN meeting | Buddy session | Habit score | Energy (1-5) |
|--------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| [Name] | ✓/✗ | ✓/✗ | ___/100 | ___ |
| ... | | | | |

HIGHLIGHTS:

- Most improved: [Name] — ___
- At-risk member: [Name] — ___
- This week's goal: ___
=========

DATA QUALITY RULES:

1. CONSISTENCY
Same definition, same process, same format every time
❌ 'About 5 connects'
✅ '5 connects exactly'

2. TIMELINESS
Collect data within 24 hours of activity
❌ 'Let me update last month's data...'
✅ 'Updated today's connects right after activity'

3. COMPLETENESS
100% of members, 100% of metrics, 100% of time periods
❌ 'I only track top performers'
✅ 'Everyone tracked, every week'

4. ACCURACY
Data should reflect reality
❌ 'I'll estimate — probably around 10 connects'
✅ 'Checked with member: exactly 8 connects'

DATA COLLECTION FREQUENCY:

REAL-TIME (As happens):
- Orders: Auto-synced from Droppii
- New member joins: Immediate entry
- Habit score changes: Daily update

DAILY:
- Leader connects: End of day count
- Team activity: Quick check
- Urgent alerts: At-risk members

WEEKLY (Sunday 30 min):
- Full PSN metrics compilation
- Weekly report to team
- Dashboard update
- Planning for next week

MONTHLY (Month end):
- Comprehensive analysis
- PSN health assessment (Cửu Địa)
- Sub-leader evaluation
- Strategy adjustment

QUARTERLY:
- Full business review
- Financial P&L
- Strategic planning session
- Goal setting for next quarter

DATA ENTRY BEST PRACTICES:

1. TEMPLATE EVERYTHING
Use templates for every report. Reduces thinking, increases consistency.

2. BATCH PROCESSING
Collect data in batches, not one-by-one.
- 30 min Sunday = compile all weekly data at once
- vs. 5 min × 6 days = same time, less efficient

3. DELEGATE DATA ENTRY
- Members enter their own data (connects, orders)
- Leader only collects and analyzes
- Use Zalo forms, Google Forms for easy entry

4. VERIFY RANDOM SAMPLES
- Check 10% of entries for accuracy
- If error rate > 5%, retrain collection process
- Trust but verify

Action items:
1. Create weekly data collection template
2. Automate 2 data streams (orders + habit score)
3. Set up weekly data collection ritual (Sunday 30 min)
4. Delegate data entry to members where possible

lessons.title: Dashboard Design — Thiết kế bảng điều khiển
lessons.objective: Build effective dashboards that drive action, not just display numbers
lessons.content:
Dashboard = your cockpit. Good dashboard = instant situational awareness. Bad dashboard = pretty numbers that nobody acts on.

DASHBOARD PRINCIPLES:

1. ONE PAGE MAX
- Everything important on ONE screen
- No scrolling, no tabs needed for daily view
- Details accessible via drill-down

2. NORTH STAR FIRST
- Most important metric at top, largest, most prominent
- Everything else supports it

3. TRAFFIC LIGHT SYSTEM
- Green: On target / improving
- Yellow: Attention needed / slightly off
- Red: Critical / declining fast

4. ACTION TRIGGERS
- Each metric has a threshold that triggers action
- 'If response rate < 15% → review DM scripts'

5. RELEVANCE FIRST
- Show what matters to YOUR PSN
- Not generic dashboard — customize everything
- Remove anything you don't act on

PSN DASHBOARD LAYOUT:

=== PSN COMMAND DASHBOARD ===

ROW 1: NORTH STAR

│  🎯 WEEKLY ACTIVE REVENUE PRODUCERS    │

│           [Trend: ↑3 vs last week]      │

ROW 2: KEY METRICS (4 quadrants)
┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐
│ RECRUIT  │ │ REVENUE  │ │ ENGAGE   │ │ TEAM     │
│          │ │          │ │          │ │          │
│ New: ___ │ │ Rev: ___K│ │ Active:  │ │ Sub-ldr: │

│ Rate:___%│ │  AOV:___K│ │ Meet:___%│ │  Cửu Địa│
│ [Trend]  │ │ [Trend]  │ │ [Trend]  │ │ [Trend]  │

ROW 3: ACTION ITEMS
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⚠️  ACTION REQUIRED:                    │
│ • Response rate dropped 5% → review DMs│
│ • 3 members inactive 14+ days → reach out│
│ • Campaign ROI below target → optimize   │

ROW 4: TOP PERFORMERS

│ Top Earner: [Name] — ___K revenue       │
│ Most Improved: [Name] — ___% increase   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

DRILL-DOWN DESIGN:

Dashboard Level 1 (Daily):
- North Star + 4 quadrants + action items
- Updated: Real-time or daily
- Audience: Leader (daily check)

Dashboard Level 2 (Weekly):
- Level 1 + per-member table + trend chart
- Updated: Weekly
- Audience: Leader + sub-leaders

Dashboard Level 3 (Monthly):
- Level 2 + cohort analysis + forecast
- Updated: Monthly
- Audience: Full PSN (summarized)

DASHBOARD TOOLS:

Free tier options:
- Google Sheets: Simple, shareable, familiar
- Notion: Databases + views, team collaboration
- Zalo OA + Sheet: Push notifications + data
- Mekong CLI dashboard: Built-in PSN tracking

Paid options (when PSN grows):
- Tableau: Advanced visualizations
- Power BI: Microsoft ecosystem
- Mixpanel: Product analytics
- Custom: Build your own with CF Workers + D1

DASHBOARD DESIGN CHECKLIST:

Before finalizing dashboard:
- [ ] Can you read it in under 30 seconds?
- [ ] Does North Star stand out?
- [ ] Are all metrics actionable?
- [ ] Do traffic lights reflect true status?
- [ ] Are action items clear and specific?
- [ ] Is drill-down available for details?
- [ ] Is it updated frequently enough to act on?
- [ ] Is it accessible to team members who need it?

COMMON DASHBOARD MISTAKES:

❌ Too many metrics: 20+ metrics = nobody looks at any
❌ Vanity metrics: Pretty but useless
❌ No action triggers: Numbers without next steps
❌ Too complex: Requires training to understand
❌ Infrequent updates: Data is 2 weeks old when you look at it
❌ One-size-fits-all: Leader dashboard ≠ team dashboard

Action items:
1. Design your PSN dashboard (use template above)
2. Choose tool and set up dashboard
3. Connect data sources (auto + manual)
4. Create Level 1 (daily) view first, expand later

lessons.title: Trend Analysis — Phân tích xu hướng
lessons.objective: Analyze trends to predict future và make proactive decisions
lessons.content:
Trend analysis = looking at data over time to see patterns. Patterns predict future.

TREND TYPES:

1. UPWARD TREND 📈
Consistent increase over time
Example: 'Connects/day increased from 5 to 15 over 3 months'
Action: Accelerate, invest more, ride the wave

2. DOWNWARD TREND 📉
Consistent decrease over time
Example: 'Revenue dropped from 2M to 800K over 6 weeks'
Action: Investigate root cause, fix before it compounds

3. FLAT/STABLE TREND ➡️
No significant change
Example: 'Members steady at 25 for 2 months'
Action: Need catalyst — campaign, new approach

4. SEASONAL TREND 📊📉📈
Cyclical pattern repeating over time
Example: 'Revenue peaks in Dec-Tết, drops in Feb-Mar'
Action: Plan campaigns around cycles, build buffers

5. VOLATILE/NOISY TREND 📈📉📈📉
No clear pattern, random fluctuations
Example: 'Connects: 10, 3, 15, 5, 12, 2...'
Action: Look at longer timeframe, or data quality issue

TREND ANALYSIS TECHNIQUES:

MOVING AVERAGE:
Smooth out noise to see real trend
- 7-day moving average: Daily metric averaged over 7 days
- 30-day moving average: Weekly metric averaged over 30 days
- Use: Identify real direction vs random fluctuation

Example:
Daily connects: 10, 15, 5, 20, 3, 18, 12
7-day MA: (10+15+5+20+3+18+12)/7 = 11.9
Next: Drop oldest (10), add newest (?) → smooth trend line

SEASONALITY ANALYSIS:

Vietnam-specific patterns:
- Tết (Jan-Feb): Revenue down, networking up
- Post-Tết (Feb-Mar): Slow restart
- Q2 (Apr-Jun): Building momentum
- Summer (Jul-Aug): Mixed (travel vs business)
- Q4 (Oct-Dec): Strong finish, year-end buying

Adjust expectations based on seasonality:
- 'July revenue is 30% below June — but that's normal for summer'
- 'December target should be 150% of average'

YEAR-OVER-YEAR (YoY) COMPARISON:
Most accurate comparison:
- 'Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025'
- Removes seasonal effects
- Shows true growth

TREND INDICATORS:

Leading indicators to watch:

1. CONNECT RATE TREND
- Trend up → More recruits coming
- Trend down → Need to address outreach quality
- Trigger: If 2-week trend down > 20%, review DM scripts

2. HABIT SCORE TREND
- Trend up → Members becoming more engaged
- Trend down → Members losing motivation
- Trigger: If PSN average drops 5+ points, leader intervention

3. RESPONSE RATE TREND
- Trend up → Messaging improving
- Trend down → Audience fatigue or poor targeting
- Trigger: If 3-week trend down, A/B test new approaches

4. REVENUE PER MEMBER TREND
- Trend up → Members getting better at business
- Trend down → Product issues, market changes, or training gaps
- Trigger: If 4-week trend down, review product training

5. RETENTION RATE TREND
- Trend up → PSN becoming stickier
- Trend down → Onboarding or experience problems
- Trigger: If monthly retention < 70%, urgent review

TREND FORECASTING:

Simple forecast: Extend current trend
- 'Connects/day grew 2/day per month for 3 months'
- 'Next month: +6/day → 18 connects/day'

Adjusted forecast: Trend + known factors
- 'Base forecast: 18 connects/day'
- '+ Campaign in Week 3: +5 connects'
- '- Summer slowdown: -3 connects'
- 'Adjusted: 20 connects/day'

Action items:
1. Plot 3-month trend for your top 3 metrics
2. Identify seasonal patterns affecting your PSN
3. Set up trend monitoring (weekly check)
4. Create forecast for next quarter based on current trends

lessons.title: Decision Frameworks — Khuôn khổ ra quyết định
lessons.objective: Apply structured decision-making frameworks using data
lessons.content:
Data without decisions = useless. Decisions without data = gambling. Combine both = power.

DECISION FRAMEWORK 1: HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN DECISION

Step 1: STATE THE HYPOTHESIS
'If we [action], then [outcome] because [reason]'
Example: 'If we increase connects from 10 to 15/day, then recruits will increase by 30% because we're reaching more prospects'

Step 2: IDENTIFY SUCCESS METRIC
What number proves the hypothesis right?
Example: 'Recruits go from 5 to 6.5/month'

Step 3: SET THRESHOLD
What's the minimum improvement to justify the action?
Example: 'If recruits increase by 15%+, keep 15 connects/day'

Step 4: RUN EXPERIMENT
Execute with measurement, minimum 2 weeks

Step 5: EVALUATE
Did outcome match hypothesis?
- Yes: Scale the approach
- No: Learn why, revise hypothesis
- Inconclusive: Run longer, adjust approach

DECISION FRAMEWORK 2: DECISION TREE

For complex decisions with multiple branches:

Example: 'Should we run a recruitment campaign?'

Is PSN stable (all systems working)?
├── NO → Fix systems first (M7 basics)
└── YES → Continue
    Is team capacity available (not overloaded)?
    ├── NO → Wait 2 weeks
    └── YES → Continue
        Is there a market opportunity (event, season)?
        ├── NO → Regular growth is fine
        └── YES → Continue
            Do we have budget (time + money)?
            ├── NO → Low-cost campaign only
            └── YES → Run full campaign

Decision trees remove emotion from decisions.

DECISION FRAMEWORK 3: OODA LOOP (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act)

Military decision cycle, perfect for fast-changing MLM environment:

OBSERVE: What's happening?
- Revenue down 20% this week
- 3 members inactive
- Campaign just ended

ORIENT: What does it mean?
- Campaign end → natural drop
- 3 inactive → need follow-up
- Revenue drop might continue

DECIDE: What should we do?
- Run retention campaign (target inactive members)
- Start new content series
- Increase team connects

ACT: Execute decision
- Send retention messages today
- Schedule content for this week
- Brief team on connect target
- Then OBSERVE again → loop continues

OODA speed advantage:
Faster OODA loop = competitive advantage.
- Slow leader: Observe (week) → Orient (week) → Decide (week) → Act (week) = 1 month cycle
- Fast leader: O (day) → O (day) → D (day) → A (day) = 4 day cycle
- Fast leader adapts 7x faster

DECISION FRAMEWORK 4: COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS

For decisions involving investment:

| Option | Cost | Benefit | ROI | Risk |
|--------|------|---------|-----|------|
| Run campaign | 200K, 20 hrs | 2M revenue | 900% | Medium |
| Hire VA | 3M/mo | 5M revenue | 67% | Low |
| Train team | 50K, 10 hrs | 300K revenue | 500% | Low |
| Do nothing | 0 | 0 | 0 | HIGH (opportunity cost) |

Rule: Choose option with highest expected value = Benefit × Probability - Cost

DECISION FRAMEWORK 5: PRE-MORTEM

Before making big decision, imagine it failed:
'It's 3 months from now. This campaign was a disaster. Why?'

Brainstorm failure reasons:
- Team didn't execute properly
- Timing was wrong (holiday)
- Offer wasn't compelling
- Budget ran out
- External factor (competitor launched)

Then: How do we prevent each failure?
- Team rehearsal before launch
- Calendar check before scheduling
- Pre-test offer with 5 prospects
- Contingency budget
- Monitor competitor activity

Pre-mortem = best insurance policy for decisions.

Action items:
1. Apply hypothesis framework to your next decision
2. Create decision tree for 1 common decision in your PSN
3. Practice OODA loop: Observe → Orient → Decide → Act in next 48 hours

lessons.title: Predictive Analytics — Dự báo xu hướng
lessons.objective: Build simple predictive models for member behavior and PSN performance
lessons.content:
Predictive analytics = using past data to predict future. Simple models, powerful insights.

PREDICTIVE MODEL 1: MEMBER CHURN RISK

Factors that predict member leaving:

| Factor | Weight | Points |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Habit score < 40 | High | +3 |
| 0 connects in 7 days | High | +3 |
| 0 orders in 21 days | High | +2 |
| Missed 2+ PSN meetings | Medium | +2 |
| No buddy session in 14 days | Medium | +1 |
| Negative feedback in 1:1 | High | +3 |
| M1 not completed in 30 days | Medium | +2 |
| PSN health score declining | High | +2 |

Risk scoring:
0-3 points: Low risk (green) — Normal engagement
4-6 points: Medium risk (yellow) — Monitor, gentle check-in
7-10 points: High risk (orange) — Active intervention needed
11+ points: Critical risk (red) — Leader intervention, likely to leave

Action based on risk:
Green: Standard support
Yellow: Extra encouragement, check in
Orange: 1:1 coaching, address specific issue
Red: Urgent leader intervention, possible PIP

PREDICTIVE MODEL 2: RECRUITMENT FORECAST

Formula:
Recruits next month = (Connects/day × 30) × Response rate × Presentation rate × Conversion rate

Example:
(10 connects/day × 30) × 15% response × 50% presentation × 20% conversion
= 300 × 0.15 × 0.5 × 0.2 = 4.5 recruits/month

Adjusting for improvement:
If connects go to 15/day: 450 × 0.15 × 0.5 × 0.2 = 6.75 recruits
If response rate improves to 20%: 450 × 0.20 × 0.5 × 0.2 = 9 recruits

This model tells you: 'To get 10 recruits, I need either 15 connects/day OR 20% response rate.'

PREDICTIVE MODEL 3: REVENUE FORECAST

Formula:
Revenue = Active members × Revenue per active member × Weeks

Example:
25 active members × 200K/week × 4 weeks = 20M/month

Growth projection:
- Month 1: 25 members, 20M/month
- Month 2: 30 members (+5 recruits), 24M/month
- Month 3: 36 members (+6 recruits), 28.8M/month
- Month 6: 50 members, 40M/month

With retention factored in:
- 10% monthly attrition = need 3+ recruits/month just to maintain
- 5% monthly attrition = need 2+ recruits/month

PREDICTIVE MODEL 4: PSN GROWTH TRAJECTORY

Growth rate formula:
Monthly growth rate = (New recruits - Attrition) / Current size × 100%

Example:
(5 recruits - 2 left) / 25 members = 12% monthly growth

Doubling time (Rule of 72):
72 / Monthly growth rate = Months to double
72 / 12 = 6 months to double from 25 to 50 members

Different growth rates:
- 5%/month: 14 months to double (slow)
- 10%/month: 7 months to double (good)
- 20%/month: 3.6 months to double (fast)
- 30%/month: 2.4 months to double (very fast)

PREDICTIVE MODEL 5: CAMPAIGN SUCCESS PREDICTION

Based on pre-campaign metrics:

Success indicators:
- Team connects/day > 15: High success probability
- PSN health score > 50: Good foundation
- 5+ warm prospects: Real pipeline
- Leader energy score > 7/10: Can drive campaign

Success probability:
| Conditions | Probability |
|------------|-------------|
| All 4 met | 80%+ success |
| 3 of 4 met | 60% success |
| 2 of 4 met | 40% success |
| 1 or fewer | <20% — don't campaign yet |

Action items:
1. Build churn risk scorecard for your members
2. Set up recruitment forecast formula
3. Calculate current PSN growth trajectory
4. Use pre-campaign checklist before next campaign

lessons.title: Data Quality & Governance — Quản trị dữ liệu
lessons.objective: Implement data quality standards and governance for reliable analytics
lessons.content:
Bad data = bad decisions. Data quality is non-negotiable.

DATA QUALITY DIMENSIONS:

1. ACCURACY
Data reflects reality
Check: Random verification — pick 10 entries, verify against source
Target: 95%+ accuracy
Fix: Double-entry for critical data, automated collection where possible

2. COMPLETENESS
All required data present
Check: Are any cells blank in weekly report?
Target: 100% completeness for core metrics
Fix: Mandatory fields, validation rules

3. CONSISTENCY
Same definition across time and people
Check: Does 'connect' mean same thing today as last month?
Target: 100% consistency
Fix: Define all terms, train all data entry people

4. TIMELINESS
Data available when needed
Check: Is last week's data available by Monday morning?
Target: Weekly data ready by Monday 9am
Fix: Automated collection, Sunday data ritual

5. UNIQUENESS
No duplicate entries
Check: Any member listed twice? Any order counted twice?
Target: 0 duplicates
Fix: Unique IDs, validation rules

6. VALIDITY
Data in correct format and range
Check: 'Orders: 150' when max possible is 10 → error
Target: 100% valid entries
Fix: Validation rules, data entry forms

DATA GOVERNANCE:

WHO owns data?

| Data Type | Owner | Access | Update Frequency |
|-----------|-------|--------|------------------|
| Revenue data | Leader | Leader + sub-leaders | Daily |
| Member activity | Members self-report | Leader | Weekly |
| Campaign metrics | Leader | Full PSN | After each campaign |
| PSN health | Leader | Full PSN | Monthly |
| Strategy data | Leader | Sub-leaders | Quarterly |

DATA DEFINITIONS (Critical):

Define EVERY term:

Connect = 'Intentional outreach to a new prospect or existing customer via any channel'
NOT: 'Said hello to friend'
NOT: 'Replied to existing customer'

Presentation = 'Business presentation showing opportunity or product'
NOT: 'Casual mention'
NOT: 'Group chat share'

Active member = 'Did at least 1 connect AND 1 order in the last 7 days'
NOT: 'Logged into app'
NOT: 'Attended PSN meeting'

Active Revenue Producer = 'Both connect AND order in last 7 days' (North Star)

Revenue = 'Net revenue from orders (after returns, discounts)'
NOT: Gross revenue
NOT: Commission earned

DATA QUALITY MONITORING:

Weekly quality check:
- [ ] All core metrics present (no blank cells)
- [ ] All numbers within valid range
- [ ] No duplicate entries
- [ ] Timestamps current (within last 7 days)
- [ ] Self-reported data matches leader observations

Monthly quality audit:
- Random 10% verification
- Definition compliance check
- Trend reasonableness check (no sudden jumps without explanation)
- Data process review

QUALITY SCORECARD:
| Dimension | This Week | Target | Status |
|-----------|----------|--------|--------|
| Completeness | ___% | 100% | 🟢/🟡/🔴 |
| Accuracy | ___% | 95% | 🟢/🟡/🔴 |
| Timeliness | ___% | 100% | 🟢/🟡/🔴 |
| Consistency | ___% | 100% | 🟢/🟡/🔴 |

Data quality = leadership quality. Leaders who care about data quality care about everything.

Action items:
1. Create data definitions document (define 10+ key terms)
2. Set up data quality weekly check
3. Define data ownership for each metric
4. Implement validation in your tracking system

lessons.title: Analytics Case Studies — Phân tích tình huống thực tế
lessons.objective: Apply analytics to real PSN scenarios through case studies
lessons.content:
Theory meets practice. Analyze 3 real scenarios using data.

CASE STUDY 1: Revenue Drop

Scenario:
PSN revenue dropped 40% in Week 3. Leader panics.

Data:
- Week 1: 4M VND
- Week 2: 3.5M VND
- Week 3: 2.1M VND
- Members: 28 (stable, no attrition)
- Connects: 120/week (up from 100)
- Orders: 5 (down from 12)
- AOV: 420K (stable, was 430K)
- New customers: 1 (down from 5)
- Customer retention: 60% (down from 80%)

Analysis:
1. Revenue = Members × Orders × AOV
- Members: Stable → not the issue
- Orders: Dropped from 12 to 5 → main cause
- AOV: Stable → product/mix unchanged

2. Why did orders drop?
- Connects UP but orders DOWN → lead quality issue
- New customers DOWN → top of funnel problem
- Customer retention DOWN → bottom of funnel problem

3. Root cause: Two problems
- Top: Lead quality degraded (more reaches, fewer conversions)
- Bottom: Customer retention worsening (repeat purchases dropping)

4. What happened 4-6 weeks ago?
- 4 weeks ago: Changed DM script
- 6 weeks ago: New product launched (different from usual)

5. Diagnosis:
- New DM script targeting wrong audience
- New product confusing to new customers

Decision:
1. Revert DM script to previous version
2. Simplify product introduction for new customers
3. Run retention campaign for lapsed customers
4. Monitor: Orders should recover in 2-3 weeks

CASE STUDY 2: Stagnant Growth

Scenario:
PSN stuck at 25 members for 4 months. Not growing, not shrinking.

Data:
- New recruits/month: 4
- Attrition/month: 4
- Growth rate: 0%
- Connects/day: 8 (below 10 target)
- Response rate: 10% (below 15% target)
- Presentation rate: 30% (below 50% target)
- PSN meeting attendance: 60%

Analysis:
1. Net growth = 0 (4 in, 4 out)
2. Attrition causes:
- 2 members: No results after 2 months
- 1 member: Moved to competitor
- 1 member: Personal reasons (job change)

3. Bottleneck analysis:
- Connects 8 vs target 10 → -20% pipeline
- Response rate 10% vs target 15% → poor quality outreach
- Presentation rate 30% vs target 50% → conversion problem
- PSN attendance 60% → engagement problem

4. Compound effect:
With current metrics: 8×30×10%×30%×20% = 1.44 recruits/month
Need: 6+ recruits/month to overcome 4 attrition = 4x improvement needed

Decision:
Priority 1: Fix connects → 12/day (50% increase)
Priority 2: Fix response rate → 15% (DM script A/B test)
Priority 3: Fix presentation rate → 50% (training)
Priority 4: Fix engagement → 80% meeting attendance (make meetings better)
Expected outcome: 12×30×15%×50%×25% = 6.75 recruits/month — overcomes 4 attrition, grows 2.75/month

CASE STUDY 3: High Activity, Low Revenue

Scenario:
Team is busy but revenue doesn't grow. Leader frustrated.

Data:
- Connects/day: 20 (above target!)
- Presentations/week: 30 (above target!)
- Orders: 4/week (below 5 target)
- Revenue: 1.2M/week (below 1.5M target)
- AOV: 300K (below 350K target)
- Repeat customers: 30% (below 50% target)
- Product mix: 80% low-price items

Analysis:
1. Activity metrics all good → problem is NOT effort
2. Revenue problem = conversion problem, not effort problem
3. AOV low → selling low-price products
4. Repeat low → no follow-up, no upselling
5. Product mix skewed → team focuses on easy sales

Root cause: Team optimizing for WRONG metric (connects) instead of revenue per connect.

Decision:
1. Shift incentive: Reward revenue, not connects
2. Train on upselling: 'Instead of selling 1 product at 300K, sell bundle at 600K'
3. Implement follow-up system: Every customer gets Day 7 follow-up
4. Track NEW metric: Revenue per connect
5. A/B test: High-price offer vs low-price offer

LESSONS FROM CASE STUDIES:

1. Always look at the WHOLE SYSTEM
Single metric improvement ≠ success. Revenue dropped despite more connects.

2. Ask 'Why' 5 times
Orders dropped → why? Response quality → why? DM script → why? Changed 4 weeks ago.

3. Activity ≠ Results
High connects ≠ high revenue. Measure outcomes, not activities.

4. Compare to targets AND trends
4M → 3.5M → 2.1M: Compare to targets AND see declining trend.

5. Look at segments
Aggregate numbers hide problems. Drill into per-member data.

Action items:
1. Analyze your PSN data using case study framework
2. Identify your biggest bottleneck (1 metric)
3. Apply 5-Why analysis to that bottleneck
4. Create action plan based on findings

lessons.title: Data-Driven Culture — Xây dựng văn hóa data
lessons.objective: Build data-driven decision culture trong PSN and team
lessons.content:
Culture eats strategy for breakfast. Data culture = everyone thinks with data, not just leader.

DATA CULTURE ELEMENTS:

1. LEADERSHIP DEMONSTRATION
Leader ALWAYS references data:
- In PSN meetings: 'Last week we had 200 connects with 15% response rate'
- In DMs: 'You're at 8 connects/day — let's get to 10'
- In planning: 'Data shows July is slow — let's plan campaign'

If leader says 'I think' without data, team will copy that behavior.

2. DATA VISIBILITY
Everyone can see key metrics:
- PSN dashboard shared in group (weekly update)
- Leaderboard posted (connects, orders, improvements)
- Public tracking of PSN goals
- Transparency = accountability

3. DATA EDUCATION
Team members understand metrics:
- Weekly: Explain 1 metric in PSN meeting ('Today we talk about response rate')
- What it means, why it matters, how to improve it
- Use simple language, visual examples

4. DATA CELEBRATION
Celebrate data improvements:
- 'Hùng improved from 5 to 12 connects this week!'
- 'Our PSN response rate went from 10% to 18%!'
- 'We hit 30 active revenue producers — new record!'

5. DATA ACTIONABILITY
Every data point has an action:
- 'Response rate dropped' → 'Let's review DM scripts today'
- '3 members inactive' → 'Reach out this week'
- 'Revenue up 20%' → 'Let's double down on what's working'

METRICS RITUALS:

DAILY (5 min): Leader checks dashboard
- North Star: Trending up or down?
- Any red alerts?
- Top priority for today?

WEEKLY (30 min): PSN meeting data segment
- Last week's numbers vs target
- Wins celebration (data-driven)
- Challenges discussion
- This week's targets

MONTHLY (1 hour): Data review session
- Full metrics review
- Trend analysis
- Sub-leader data coaching
- Strategy adjustment based on data

QUARTERLY (Half day): Data deep dive
- Full quarterly analysis
- Year-over-year comparison
- Strategic planning based on data
- Goal setting for next quarter

DATA STORYTELLING:

Data alone is boring. Data with STORY is compelling.

Bad: 'Revenue was 12M last month'
Good: 'Revenue was 12M — up 20% from 10M last month. What drove this? The flash sale campaign brought in 5M, and our 3 new members are contributing 2M. At this rate, we'll hit 20M by end of quarter.'

Storytelling structure:
1. CONTEXT: Where we are vs target
2. CHANGE: What moved the needle
3. CAUSE: Why it happened
4. IMPLICATION: What it means for future
5. ACTION: What we do next

PSN MEETING DATA SEGMENT (15 min template):

1. THE NUMBERS (3 min)
- 'Last week: ___ connects, ___ presentations, ___ orders, ___M revenue'
- 'Targets: ___ connects, ___ presentations, ___ orders, ___M revenue'
- 'Variance: +/- ___%'

2. THE WIN (5 min)
- 'Biggest win: [Member] achieved ___'
- 'What made it happen? [Specific action]'
- 'How can we replicate? [Action for everyone]'

3. THE CHALLENGE (5 min)
- 'Challenge: [Metric] below target'
- 'Why? [Root cause from data]'
- 'What do we do? [Group discussion]'

4. THE GOAL (2 min)
- 'This week's target: ___ connects, ___ orders, ___M revenue'
- 'One focus area: [Priority metric to improve]'

DATA LITERACY PROGRESSION:

Level 1: Knows numbers
- Member can read dashboard and understand basic metrics

Level 2: Understands trends
- Member can see if their metrics are improving or declining

Level 3: Makes data-driven decisions
- Member adjusts their actions based on their own data

Level 4: Teaches others with data
- Member uses data to coach their own customers/prospects

Action items:

2. Share dashboard with team (create access)
3. Start celebrating data-driven wins
4. Create simple data education: 'Metric of the week' series

lessons.title: Predictive Modeling — Mô hình dự báo
lessons.objective: Build practical predictive models for PSN optimization
lessons.content:
Predictive modeling = quantified intuition. Simple models beat complex ones for PSN scale.

PREDICTIVE MODEL 1: MEMBER LIFETIME VALUE (LTV)

Simple LTV model:
LTV = (Avg Monthly Revenue per Member) × (Avg Membership Duration in Months)

Example:
- Avg monthly orders: 2 orders/month
- Avg order value: 250K
- Avg monthly revenue: 500K
- Avg membership: 12 months
- LTV = 500K × 12 = 6M VND per member

Segment LTV:
- Active members: 12 months avg → 6M LTV
- Sub-leaders: 24 months avg → 12M LTV
- Leaders: 36 months avg → 18M LTV

Using LTV:
- Maximum CPA = LTV × 30% = 1.8M × 30% = 540K per active member
- Investment in retention: If retention program costs 100K/member and saves 20% attrition → saves 1.2M LTV per saved member

PREDICTIVE MODEL 2: CHURN PREDICTION SCORE

Input variables (0-5 each):

| Variable | 0 pts | 1 pt | 2 pts | 3 pts | 4 pts | 5 pts |
|----------|-------|------|------|------|------|------|
| Habit score | >80 | 70-79 | 60-69 | 50-59 | 40-49 | <40 |
| Connects/week | >15 | 12-14 | 8-11 | 5-7 | 2-4 | 0-1 |
| Orders/month | >5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0 |

| Last 1:1 | <7d | 7-14d | 14-21d | 21-30d | 30-45d | 45d+ |

|-------|------------|---------------------|--------|

| 6-10 | Low | 15% | Encourage, check in |
| 11-15 | Medium | 35% | Proactive engagement |
| 16-20 | High | 60% | Active intervention |
| 21-25 | Critical | 85% | Urgent, likely leaving |

PREDICTIVE MODEL 3: RECRUITMENT PIPELINE FORECAST

Pipeline stages with conversion rates:

| Stage | Count | Conv. Rate | Expected Recruits |
|-------|-------|------------|-------------------|
| Prospects reached | ___ | 25% | ___ |
| Responses received | ___ | 60% | ___ |
| Presentations done | ___ | 40% | ___ |
| Decision stage | ___ | 50% | ___ |
| Expected recruits | | | ___ |

Example with 100 prospects:
- Reached: 100 × 25% = 25 responses
- Responses: 25 × 60% = 15 presentations
- Presentations: 15 × 40% = 6 decisions
- Decisions: 6 × 50% = 3 recruits

To get 10 recruits: Need ___ prospects in pipeline
10 = P × 25% × 60% × 40% × 50%
10 = P × 0.03
P = 333 prospects needed in pipeline

This model tells you: 'To get 10 recruits this month, I need 333 prospects in my pipeline.'

Based on pre-campaign metrics:

Success indicators:

lessons.title: Advanced Analytics — Phân tích nâng cao
lessons.objective: Apply advanced analytics techniques for strategic PSN decisions
lessons.content:
Advanced analytics = finding insights that basic metrics miss.

COHORT ANALYSIS:

Group members by join month and track behavior over time:

| Cohort | Month | Month +1 | Month +2 | Month +3 | 90-day retention |
|--------|-------|----------|----------|----------|-----------------|
| Jan | 25 joined | 20 active | 15 active | 12 active | 48% |
| Feb | 20 joined | 16 active | 12 active | 10 active | 50% |
| Mar | 30 joined | 22 active | 15 active | ? | 50% (proj) |

Insights from cohort analysis:
- 'January cohort has 48% retention at 90 days'
- 'February cohort improved to 50% — onboarding changes working'
- 'March cohort tracking at 50% — on pace'
- 'We need 60% retention at 90 days to achieve net growth'

Cohort analysis answers: 'Are we getting BETTER at onboarding and retention over time?'

ATTRIBUTION MODELING:

Which channel drove which result?

First-touch attribution: 'First channel that reached member gets credit'
Last-touch attribution: 'Final channel before conversion gets credit'
Linear attribution: 'All touchpoints get equal credit'
Time-decay attribution: 'Closer touchpoints get more credit'

Example — Member Thu's journey:
1. Saw FB post (Day -14) — First touch: FB
2. Zalo DM from leader (Day -10)
3. Attended Zalo event (Day -7)
4. Personal 1:1 call (Day -3)
5. Joined PSN (Day 0) — Last touch: 1:1 call

Attribution:
- First-touch: FB (100% credit to FB)
- Last-touch: 1:1 call (100% credit to 1:1)
- Linear: FB 20%, DM 20%, Event 20%, 1:1 40%
- Time-decay: FB 10%, DM 15%, Event 25%, 1:1 50%

Recommendation: Time-decay for MLM (relationship building matters most)

Channel ROI comparison:
| Channel | Members | Cost | CPA | LTV | ROI |
|---------|---------|------|-----|-----|-----|
| Zalo DM | 15 | 0K (time) | 0K | 6M | ∞ |
| Events | 8 | 100K | 12.5K | 6M | 47,900% |
| Facebook | 5 | 50K | 10K | 6M | 59,900% |
| Referral | 3 | 20K | 6.7K | 6M | 89,400% |

Insight: Referral is best ROI. Invest more in referral systems.

CORRELATION ANALYSIS:

Find relationships between metrics:

| Metric A | Metric B | Correlation | Insight |
|----------|----------|-------------|---------|
| Connects/day | Recruits/month | +0.85 | Strong positive |
| Presentations | Revenue | +0.72 | Strong positive |
| PSN attendance | Retention | +0.68 | Moderate positive |
| Habit score | Orders | +0.55 | Moderate positive |
| Connect frequency | Response rate | -0.30 | Negative (fatigue) |
| Event frequency | Revenue | +0.40 | Moderate positive |

Correlation ≠ Causation:
- 'PSN attendance correlates with retention' — does attendance CAUSE retention or do engaged members attend more?
- Test: Randomly assign half to mandatory attendance → see if retention improves

SEGMENT ANALYSIS:

Break data by segments to find hidden insights:

By member level:
| Level | Avg Revenue | Avg Connects | Retention |
|-------|-------------|-------------|----------|
| M1 | 50K | 5 | 70% |
| M2 | 150K | 8 | 75% |
| M3 | 300K | 10 | 80% |
| M4 | 500K | 12 | 85% |

Insight: Higher levels = better metrics across the board
Action: Accelerate members through M1-M4

By join month:
| Month | 30-day retention | 90-day retention |
|-------|-----------------|-----------------|
| Jan | 85% | 48% |
| Feb | 88% | 50% |
| Mar | 90% | ? |

Insight: Retention improving over time → onboarding improvements working

By acquisition channel:
| Channel | Count | 30-day retention | 90-day retention | LTV |
|---------|-------|-----------------|-----------------|-----|
| Event | 25 | 85% | 60% | 7M |
| Zalo DM | 18 | 75% | 45% | 5M |
| FB | 10 | 70% | 40% | 4M |
| Referral | 8 | 90% | 70% | 8M |

Insight: Referral members have highest LTV — invest in referral program

Action items:
1. Conduct cohort analysis on your members (by join month)
2. Map attribution for your last 10 new members
3. Run correlation analysis on your key metrics
4. Segment analysis by member level and channel

lessons.title: Data Storytelling — Kể chuyện bằng data
lessons.objective: Communicate insights effectively through data storytelling
lessons.content:
Best analysis is worthless if you can't communicate it. Data storytelling = make data compelling.

DATA STORY STRUCTURE:

Every data story has 5 parts:

1. THE HOOK (Opening)
Grab attention with surprising or important finding.
'Our PSN hit 30 active revenue producers this week — that's a 50% increase from last month.'

2. THE CONTEXT (Where we are)
Provide background so audience understands significance.
'Two months ago we were at 15 active producers. We've been working on connects and response rates.'

3. THE EVIDENCE (What the data shows)
Present data clearly, visually, with key highlights.
[Chart showing growth trend]
'Connects went from 200/week to 450/week. Response rate from 10% to 18%. Orders from 8 to 15.'

4. THE INSIGHT (What it means)
Don't just show numbers — explain significance.
'This means our team is converting leads 2x better than before. At this rate, we'll hit 50 members by September.'

5. THE ACTION (What we do next)
Clear call to action based on data.
'This week: maintain current connects. Next month: focus on increasing AOV. Here's the plan...'

DATA VISUALIZATION PRINCIPLES:

1. RIGHT CHART FOR RIGHT MESSAGE:

| Message | Best Chart |
|---------|------------|
| Trend over time | Line chart |
| Comparison | Bar chart |
| Part of whole | Pie/Donut chart |
| Distribution | Histogram |
| Relationship | Scatter plot |
| Progress to goal | Gauge/progress bar |
| Ranking | Horizontal bar |

2. SIMPLICITY:
- Max 3-5 data series per chart
- Max 5-7 categories
- Remove chart junk (3D effects, unnecessary gridlines)
- One message per chart

3. ANNOTATION:
- Highlight key points with annotations
- 'Here's where we changed strategy'
- 'This spike was from the campaign'
- 'This dip was Tết holiday'

4. COLOR MEANING:
- Green: Good, improving, target met
- Yellow: Caution, attention needed
- Red: Bad, declining, below target
- Blue: Neutral, information

PRESENTATION TEMPLATE:

=== DATA PRESENTATION (PSN Meeting) ===

SLIDE 1: HEADLINE
'Revenue up 40% — Here's why and what's next'

SLIDE 2: THE NUMBERS
[Visual: Revenue trend chart]
'Week 1: 3M → Week 4: 4.2M'
'Monthly: 12M → 16.8M'
'Target: 15M → Actual: 16.8M (112%)'

SLIDE 3: THE DRIVERS
[Visual: Breakdown by source]
'What drove the growth:'
'• Campaign: +3M (35% of increase)'
'• New members: +2M (23%)'
'• AOV increase: +1.8M (21%)'

SLIDE 4: THE INSIGHT
'Key insight: Our campaigns are working 2x better than organic growth. We should increase campaign frequency from monthly to bi-weekly.'

SLIDE 5: THE PLAN
[Visual: Next month's plan]
'Action items:'
'• Run recruitment campaign (Week 1-2)'
'• Train team on upselling (Week 3)'
'• A/B test new DM script (ongoing)'

COMMUNICATING WITH DIFFERENT AUDIENCES:

For TEAM (PSN meeting):
- Focus on: Their contribution, team progress, clear targets
- Tone: Motivational, celebratory, clear
- Format: Simple charts, big numbers, action items
- Time: 15-20 min max

For SUB-LEADERS:
- Focus on: Their PSN performance, improvement areas
- Tone: Coaching, supportive, specific
- Format: Individual scorecards, comparison to benchmarks
- Time: 30 min per sub-leader

For UPLINE:
- Focus on: Growth rate, ROI, leadership development
- Tone: Professional, data-backed, forward-looking
- Format: Executive summary, key metrics, strategic recommendations
- Time: 10-15 min

For STRATEGIC PARTNERS:
- Focus on: Market opportunity, growth potential, partnership value
- Tone: Business-focused, opportunity-oriented
- Format: Market analysis, projections, mutual benefit

INFLUENCING THROUGH DATA:

1. START WITH THEIR CONCERN
'You're worried about revenue. Here's what data shows...'

2. SHOW, DON'T TELL
Chart beats paragraph. Let data speak.

3. BE SPECIFIC
'Revenue up 40%' not 'Revenue up significantly'

4. CONNECT TO ACTION
Every insight → one clear next step

5. USE STORIES
'Here's what happened with Hùng — he increased connects from 5 to 15, and his revenue tripled in one month.'

Action items:
1. Create 1 data presentation for next PSN meeting
2. Design 3 key charts for your dashboard
3. Practice 5-minute data storytelling
4. Prepare data story for your upline
